findings.summary: _git_report_plain only rejects assignments and git options inside the report's own command; its docstring says "A pager the configuration or the environment names without a word of this command is not seen." The same line can set that environment one command earlier. `export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=pager.ls-files GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='xargs cat'; git ls-files .env` or `export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'pager.status=xargs cat'"; git status -s .env` therefore stays quiet. Both are the F72 attack with `export` in front. With `core.fsmonitor=…` the same works without a terminal, and the docstring itself names fsmonitor as something that "runs a program outright". Fix: turn down a git report on any line that has an `export`, `declare -x`, `typeset -x` or a `GIT_*`/`PAGER` assignment in an earlier command. Add F72-style rows with `export` in front.

_REPORT_DIRS includes `/usr/local/bin` and `/opt/homebrew/bin`. Homebrew installs leave these folders writable by the user, so `ln -s /bin/cat /opt/homebrew/bin/ls; /opt/homebrew/bin/ls .env` stays silent, which is the F64 case the sixth round meant to close. A bare `ls` found through PATH has the same exposure, so the gap is smaller than F64, but these two folders are not system folders in the sense the comment gives. Either limit the set to `/bin` and `/usr/bin` or record this as a known residual.

The diff deliberately makes harmless commands ask where they were silent before: `echo }`, report names with a path outside the system folders, any git option other than `-C`/`--no-pager`/`-P`, any assignment in front of git, a carriage return on the line, and `case` inside a quoted substitution (`--ignore-case`). The "price" rows in tools/guard/tests/test_table_forms.py document these. The diff adds no DECISIONS.md line for these choices, and the repo's rules ask for one per decision.

summary: No tests are removed or weakened. The diff adds row tables, a fuzz test of the mask, and tests that `unread` is required and that `reader_pass` sets the `read` mark. The timed bound uses HOOK_BUDGET_S, which is about 290 times the measured run time. I found no secrets. The new strict reading only adds asks, apart from one gap. The seventh-round pager check reads only the git command's own words, so a pager set by an earlier `export` on the same line still leaves the report quiet. That is the same attack the F72 rows pin, written one step apart. Also, two of the folders treated as system folders can be written without sudo on macOS. The new asks this round adds on harmless commands are a policy choice, and the diff records none of them in DECISIONS.md.
